topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Speed-Cost Balance
explanation: The memory hierarchy is a tiered storage architecture designed to optimize system performance by balancing access speed and storage cost. It places smaller, faster, and more expensive volatile memory (registers, L1/L2 cache) closest to the CPU, while larger, slower, and cheaper storage (main memory, secondary storage) resides further down. This structure exploits the principle of locality of reference, ensuring that frequently or recently accessed data resides in the higher, faster levels. Caching strategies govern the automated movement and replication of data between these levels to minimize effective memory access latency and maximize processor utilization.
